request.prompt: Which humanoid robots are commercially available?

result.text:
As of October 2026, there are several commercially available humanoid robots, ranging from relatively affordable research platforms to full-size industrial robots designed for factories, warehouses and service environments.

The important distinction is that commercially available does not necessarily mean fully autonomous or ready to replace a human worker. Some can be purchased directly, others are sold through enterprise contracts, and some are only available for pilot projects.

1. Humanoid robots available to buy

These are among the most interesting options where actual purchasing or commercial ordering is possible.

1. Unitree G1

Available to order

Manufacturer: Unitree Robotics (China)

Price: from approximately $13,500

Height: approximately 1.27 m

Applications: research, education, manipulation, AI development.

One of the most accessible full-body humanoid platforms.

Manufacturer website

2. Unitree R1

Commercial offering

Manufacturer: Unitree Robotics

Advertised starting price: approximately $4,900

Height: approximately 1.23 m

Applications: education, research and robotics development.

More affordable, but less capable than the G1.

Manufacturer website

3. Unitree H2

Commercial offering

Manufacturer: Unitree Robotics

Advertised price: approximately $29,900

Height: approximately 1.8 m

Applications: research, industrial development and advanced robotics.

4. Fourier GR-1

Commercial offering

Manufacturer: Fourier Intelligence (China)

Price: varies by configuration; approximately $150,000 reported.

Height: approximately 1.65–1.75 m, depending on configuration.

Applications: research, healthcare robotics and human-robot interaction.

Manufacturer website

5. AgiBot A2

Commercial deployment

Manufacturer: AgiBot (China)

Applications: reception, customer interaction and service tasks.

Commercial production and deployment are underway.

Pricing generally requires a commercial enquiry.

Manufacturer website

2. Industrial humanoid robots available to businesses

These are particularly relevant for manufacturing, logistics and material handling. They are generally sold through enterprise agreements rather than conventional online shops.

6. Digit

Commercially deployed

Manufacturer: Agility Robotics (USA)

Height: approximately 1.75 m

Applications: warehouse logistics, tote handling and material movement.

Customers include GXO and other industrial operators.

Available through enterprise commercial arrangements.

Manufacturer website

7. Walker S2

Commercial production

Manufacturer: UBTECH Robotics (China)

Applications: factory operations, logistics and manufacturing.

Notable feature: autonomous battery-swapping capability.

Primarily enterprise procurement.

Manufacturer website

8. Apollo

Manufacturer: Apptronik (USA)

Height: approximately 1.73 m

Applications: manufacturing, warehouse work and material handling.

Commercial pilots and customer partnerships, rather than general retail availability.

Manufacturer website

9. Figure 02 / Figure 03

Manufacturer: Figure AI (USA)

Applications: industrial assembly, material handling and general-purpose manipulation.

Demonstrated in BMW manufacturing operations.

Customer pilots and production ramp-up; not a generally orderable retail product.

Manufacturer website

10. 4NE-1

Commercial programme

Manufacturer: NEURA Robotics (Germany)

Applications: industrial assistance, manufacturing and human-robot collaboration.

Particularly interesting for the European market.

Reservations and commercial procurement programmes; confirm delivery status and configuration.

Manufacturer website

3. Other commercially offered humanoids

4. High-profile robots not generally available to purchase

These are often presented as commercially available, but there are important restrictions.

Optimus — Tesla

Intended for manufacturing and eventually domestic tasks.

Primarily deployed within Tesla's own operations.

No established general customer purchasing programme.

6. My assessment

The market currently falls into three broad categories:

Affordable development platforms: Unitree is particularly interesting because it makes humanoid hardware accessible to universities, developers and smaller robotics companies.

Industrial working robots: Agility Digit, UBTECH Walker and Figure are among the most interesting platforms for industrial deployment.

General-purpose humanoids: Tesla Optimus, 1X NEO and Figure represent the ambition to develop robots capable of working in environments designed for humans, but their commercial maturity varies substantially.

One important consideration: purchasing a humanoid robot does not automatically provide autonomous task execution. Software, training, integration, safety systems and ongoing support can be just as important as the hardware.

What I would investigate next

If the objective is to identify a robot that can actually be purchased and put to work, I would narrow the comparison to these five:

I can also prepare a detailed comparison of the commercially available humanoid robots, including purchase prices, payload, walking speed, battery life, degrees of freedom, manipulation capabilities, autonomy and availability from European suppliers, with particular attention to the German market.
